answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a token bond before it may trade or vote in a terrace market. Random, time-limited tasks are cross-checked: an honest agent’s result should echo across peers, while a fabricated cluster is exposed when its mirror answers correlate too closely. Proven collusion or duplicate control slashes the bond, so creating thousands of identities requires thousands of deposits and makes attack losses expensive.
